problemStatement: Measured on the executed DockQ development pilot, the attested v0.5 evidence ordinal ranks near-native poses at target-macro AUROC 0.574180187644, against 0.5 for an all-tied baseline.
A single measurement the ordinal does not consult, interface burial, reaches 0.754144372319 on the same poses under the same tie-aware metric.
The ordinal is nearly constant on this distribution: 309 of 360 retained poses are 'limited' and 4 are 'supported', leaving almost no ranking resolution.
Interface burial is absent from the ordinal's inputs. Within the 'limited' bucket alone, half-delta-SASA spans 38 to 4880 square angstroms.

The 'supported' tier requires severeClashCount === 0, treating overlap burden as monotonic in pose error. It is not: poses with zero severe overlaps are DockQ-positive 23.1% of the time while poses with four or more are positive 67.4% of the time, because near-native packing trips the 0.6 angstrom overlap threshold while a pose rotated off the interface stops contacting the receptor at all.
96.9% of CAPRI high or medium development poses carry at least one severe overlap and are therefore barred from the 'supported' tier irrespective of their geometry.
designRationale: Ranking is continuous rather than bucketed, removing the resolution loss that caps the ordinal near chance.
The ranking signal is one physically meaningful quantity passed through unchanged, so the candidate carries no coefficient that five correlated development targets could overfit.
Overlap burden and numbering availability are reported beside the ranking as non-gating cautions, because neither is monotonic in pose error on this distribution.
Assessability fails closed: an interface below the structural minimums, or whose burial could not be computed, sorts to the bottom rather than receiving an optimistic default.

Combining burial with contact count or an overlap penalty was explored on the development pilot and rejected. Neither variant moved target-macro AUROC by more than the spread expected across five correlated targets, and both would have introduced fitted terms.

developmentEvidence.baselineReproduced: The replay harness reproduces the recorded v0.5 evidence-ordinal and delta-SASA arms to twelve decimal places, so the comparison is like-for-like.

requiredPromotionGates: Pass candidate-specific assessability, fail-closed, passthrough, non-gating-caution, and deterministic-ordering regressions.
Reproduce the recorded v0.5 evidence-ordinal and delta-SASA development arms exactly, so any future change to the candidate is measured against an unchanged baseline.
Run the public 17-structure coordinate panel and account for every ranking change against the v0.5 ordinal.
Specify, in advance and in writing, the ranking arm and cutoff to be reported from the hard-decoy holdout, before that holdout is executed.
Execute the hard-decoy holdout exactly once and report the result irrespective of outcome.
Create a new v0.6 implementation attestation and preserve all v0.5 attestations byte-for-byte.
Route production ranking to the candidate only after the preceding gates pass.
knownLimitations: The development pilot is a native-derived local rigid-body perturbation grid with 63.6% positives. It is an easier distribution than the prospectively specified hard-decoy protocol, and candidate performance is expected to fall on harder decoys.
Five targets provide far less independent information than 360 poses suggests, because poses drawn from one complex are strongly correlated.
Target-macro AUROC of 0.754 is a weak ranking prior, not a reliable filter. It does not justify presenting the ranking as a verdict.

The candidate's ordering is identical to the delta-SASA arm already recorded in the development pilot. Its contribution is adopting that signal as the product ranking with explicit assessability and non-gating cautions, not the discovery of a new signal.
Burial scales with interface size, so scores are not comparable between different complexes.
